subject: latent variable name collapse with observed variable?

messages.author: c9805acab0e9d56d
messages.subject: latent variable name collapse with observed variable?
parts:
Hi,
I just upgraded lavaan from 0.6-5 to 0.6-6 and I got this problem. I did an SEM model (path+measurement) with 0.6-5, which was great. But when I upgraded to 0.6-6, I used the same code but an error message came out, which said "some latent variable names collapse with observed variable" and lavaan gave the two "wrong" variables. However, they are latent variables, not observed variables. I don't know why 0.6-6 can't even tell which is an observed variable or a latent variable. Can anyone help how to solve this problem? Obviously I can't go back to 0.6-5.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: latent variable name collapse with observed variable?
parts: "some latent variable names collapse with observed variable" and lavaan gave the two "wrong" variables. However, they are latent variables, not observed variables.

Are you sure those variable names aren't also in your data= set?  Check with something like 

c("latent1","latent2") %in% names(myData)

where you put the 2 actual latent variable names in the first vector, and the actual name of your data.frame in place of myData.
Obviously I can't go back to 0.6-5

It might have been resolved already, try installing the development version:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/development.html

If the problem persists, you can actually go back to 0.6-5 (or even older versions, if there is a reason to) by downloading the "tarball" with source files from CRAN's archive:

https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/lavaan/ 

Then installing it using 

install.packages("lavaan_0.6-5.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")

But if this is really an error because those latent names are not anywhere in your data, then it is a bug that should be fixed.  It would help (in that case) if you could report it on GitHub, and provide a reproducible example (with even just a few rows of data) to track down the problem.

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues

Terrence D. Jorgensen
